titel: Remembering Wendell Berry With Those Who Know Him

einzeiler: Remembering the life and literary legacy of Wendell Berry with those who knew him.
kurzfassung: Host David Kern speaks with Martin Cothran and Alan Cornett, two people who knew Wendell Berry well. They share personal memories, discuss his writing habits and precision with language, and recommend where readers should start with his work. The conversation highlights Berry's character, his deep connection to Kentucky, and his lasting literary impact.
stichpunkte: Martin Cothran and Alan Cornett share personal recollections of knowing Wendell Berry.
Berry was known for his extraordinary verbal exactitude and obsessive attention to precision.
Cothran recommends starting with the short story collection Fidelity and the novels Jaber Crow or Hannah Coulter.
Berry maintained a strict daily writing routine in his long-legged house overlooking the Kentucky River.
Despite his literary fame, Berry remained grounded, approachable, and deeply connected to his local community.
Alan Cornett discusses Berry's skepticism toward technology and computers dating back to the 1980s.
Both guests highlight Berry's warmth, storytelling ability, and great sense of humor in private interactions.
The guests reflect on the overwhelming outpouring of tributes across the internet following Berry's passing.

clips.text: Martin Cothran notes that Wendell Berry spoke with extreme deliberation, carefully weighing every single word he uttered even in casual settings.
Martin Cothran explains that he routinely keeps copies of the short story collection Fidelity in his car trunk to give to readers new to Berry's work.

clips.hook: A joke about how he understood women
clips.text: Martin Cothran recalls an event where Wendell Berry deadpan joked that he understood women so well because he identified as trans before laughing.
Alan Cornett describes how Wendell Berry and his wife avoided air conditioning and carefully monitored household waste.

clips.hook: Fitting in at the country store porch
clips.text: Alan Cornett observes that if one removed his writing entirely, Wendell Berry would have felt completely at home telling stories on a country store porch.

beschreibung:
In this second tribute episode to Wendell Berry, Martin Cothran and Alan Cornett join the show to share what it was like to know Berry the man, not just the great literary figure.
